title: Wholesale prices up 0.3% in October; annual rate hits 6.5%
h1: U.S. wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, lifting the annual rate to 6.5%, the highest since late 2022
description: The Producer Price Index rose 0.3% in October 2026 and 6.5% over 12 months, the Labor Department said November 13. Goods prices were up 10.2% from a year ago.
standfirst: The monthly gain was smaller than forecast and far below September's jump. The 12-month rate still climbed to its highest level in nearly four years, three weeks before the Federal Reserve meets.
keywords: October 2026 PPI, producer price index October 2026, wholesale inflation 6.5 percent, final demand goods prices, Fed December 2026 meeting, truck freight prices
takeaways: The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October after a 1.4% jump in September; economists had expected 0.4%.
Over 12 months the index was up 6.5%, the largest rise since November 2022. Goods prices were up 10.2%.
The Fed meets December 8 and 9. The November wholesale price report is due December 15.
body: Prices paid to U.S. producers rose 0.3% in October, a much smaller gain than September's 1.4% jump, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Friday, November 13. Over the past 12 months the Producer Price Index for final demand was up 6.5%, the largest rise since a 7.4% increase in November 2022. Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had expected a 0.4% monthly gain, CNBC reported.

Goods did most of the work. Prices for final demand goods rose 0.5% in the month and were 10.2% higher than a year earlier. Food prices climbed 1.3%. Energy slipped 0.1% after surging in September, with diesel fuel down 7.9%. Basic organic chemicals rose 3.9%.

Services prices rose 0.2%, a fifth straight monthly increase. More than 80% of that gain came from truck freight, where prices jumped 3.9%, the bureau said. Margins for wholesalers and retailers, which the report calls trade services, fell 0.2%.
A narrower measure that leaves out food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% for a second month and was up 4.9% over the year.
What does it mean for interest rates?

The report follows Tuesday's consumer price figures, which showed a 0.4% rise in October. The Federal Reserve's next meeting is December 8 and 9, and markets fully price in an increase of at least a quarter point, according to CNBC.

Policymakers worry that price pressure from the Iran war, higher fuel costs and tariffs is spreading through the economy, CNBC reported. "Inflation is rising; it's proved far more persistent than we predicted at the beginning from the supply shocks," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee told the network.
Stock futures added to their gains after the release and Treasury yields were mixed, CNBC said.
The November wholesale price report is scheduled for Tuesday, December 15, a week after the Fed's decision. Monthly figures in this series are often revised.
